articles.title: House on the Northern Coast of Sao Paulo  / André Vainer Arquitetos
articles.summary: Designed for six siblings and their families, this spacious seafront house occupies a corner lot in a housing development tract designed by the brilliant Lúcio Costa. The generous scale of the house called for an L-shaped layout, which allows most of the rooms to face both the sea and the pool and garden enclosed within the site. A separate caretaker’s house is located near the street entrance. Built on a previously filled site, the house stretches in a long, linear form between the required setbacks imposed by local building regulations.

articles.title: Public Interest Design in South Africa
articles.summary: This book presents salient examples of architectural projects and practices in South Africa since 1994 that collectively subscribe to the paradigm shift towards Public Interest Design. Despite radical political transformation in the country, the people of South Africa remain adversely affected by the socio-spatial legacies of a segregated urban landscape. The contributions by architects to address these challenges go largely unnoticed and remain a marginalised practice, even within the mainstream profession.

articles.title: Metaxis: A Collection of Ideas and Objects by FUTUREFORMS

METAXIS explores what happens in between: between ideas, objects, spaces, and ways of seeing. It reflects on the dynamic state of being in the middle of things, a shifting tension or oscillation rather than a fixed condition. The exhibited projects move fluidly between perception and imagination, inside and outside, presence and absence, art and architecture. articles.title: Cinema Studio Namibe: Reviving a Tropical Modernist Icon in Angola
articles.summary: What sustains the purpose of architecture that has never been occupied? For decades, this was the question surrounding the Namibe Cinema-Studio, built on the coast of Angola in 1973. Conceived as a film screening venue, the building remained closed and abandoned, never fulfilling the role for which it was created. Yet it withstood the passage of time, becoming an icon of the Angolan landscape and architecture , until finally screening its first film nearly fifty years later.
